test_title: PYST 23: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - GA (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:
Assertion (A): The Buddha sculptures of the Gandhara School show Hellenistic features.
Reason (R): The Buddha head from this school has curly hair and shows typical Hellenistic elements.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Assertion (A)** states that the **Buddha sculptures** of the **Gandhara School** show **Hellenistic features**. This school of art flourished in the **northwestern part** of the Indian subcontinent (modern-day **Pakistan and Afghanistan**) and was heavily influenced by **Greek and Roman** styles due to its proximity to the **Hellenistic world**. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.***

• **Reason (R)** explains that the **Buddha head** from this school features **curly hair** and other typical **Hellenistic elements**. The **Gandhara Buddha** is often depicted with facial features resembling the **Greek God Apollo**, including a **sharp nose**, **defined lips**, and **wavy hair** tied in a topknot known as the **Ushnisha**. ***Hence, Reason (R) is correct.***

• The specific physical traits mentioned in **Reason (R)**, such as the **anatomical accuracy** and **curly hair**, are the direct reasons why the **Gandhara School** is classified as having **Hellenistic** or **Greco-Buddhist** features.

• The combination of **Buddhist themes** with **foreign techniques** of execution is the hallmark of this school, which emerged during the **1st Century BC** and reached its peak during the **Kushan Empire** under **King Kanishka**.

• ***Hence, both A and R are true, and R provides the correct explanation for A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Origins and Patronage**:

• The **Gandhara School of Art** developed during the **1st Century BC to 4th Century AD**.

• It received significant patronage from the **Kushan Dynasty**, particularly **King Kanishka**, who was a great promoter of **Mahayana Buddhism**.

• The major centers of this art were **Taxila**, **Peshawar**, and **Bagram**.

• **Materials and Techniques**:

• The early sculptures of the **Gandhara School** were primarily made using **bluish-grey schist stone**.

• In the later phases (around the **3rd and 4th Century AD**), **stucco** (a type of lime-plaster) and **mud** were increasingly used for creating figurines and reliefs.

• The style is characterized by **realistic anatomy**, **muscular representations**, and **heavy drapery** with folds, similar to **Roman togas**.

• **Comparison with Mathura School**:

• Unlike the **Gandhara School**, which was **hybrid** in nature, the **Mathura School** was purely **indigenous** and developed around the same period in **Uttar Pradesh**.

• The **Mathura School** used **spotted red sandstone** as its primary material.

• In **Mathura art**, the **Buddha** was depicted as **stout** and **smiling**, focusing more on spiritual inner joy rather than **Hellenistic physical perfection**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Hellenistic Influence**: The influence of **Alexander the Great’s** conquests and the subsequent **Indo-Greek kingdoms** led to the **amalgamation** of **Greek art** with **Indian religious themes**.

• **Physical Attributes**: The **Buddha** in **Gandhara art** is often shown with a **halo** (Prabhamandala), which sometimes features **geometric patterns**, and his **ears are elongated** to signify his previous life as a **Prince (Siddhartha)** who wore heavy jewelry.

• **Artistic Legacy**: This school is credited with the **first anthropomorphic representation** of the **Buddha** (depicting him in human form), as earlier **Hinayana** traditions used **symbols** like the **Bodhi tree**, **footprints**, or an **empty throne**.

• **Mudras**: The sculptures often depict the **Buddha** in various **Mudras** (hand gestures) such as **Abhaya Mudra** (fearlessness), **Dharmachakra Mudra** (teaching), and **Dhyana Mudra** (meditation).
